toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Last week's 5xx rate of 0.41% is within the service's normal range. Over the previous 26 weeks the mean was 0.354% and the upper edge of the normal band was 0.482%. Three earlier weeks were higher, and each was investigated with no fault found. The error budget burn was 0.82x, well under the 2x paging threshold. Bookings and customer complaints did not move. The dashboard count matches a raw log recount, so this isn't a counting artefact.

The "new pods error at twice the rate" finding is a rollout warm-up effect. The same gap appeared in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy, and it comes from cold caches causing a few timeouts (10–20 errors per rollout). It says nothing about v4.18 itself. I can't rule out a small effect from v4.18, the replica move or partner-sync month-end traffic, but nothing needs explaining.

Recommendation: don't roll back, don't move the replica back, and keep all alerting on. Muting the burn-rate page for a month would remove the protection that would catch a real problem. Record the week as normal and apply the standard check to next week. If next week exceeds 0.48%, or the burn-rate page fires, open an incident and look at the replica move and partner-sync timing. I'm fairly confident in this, not certain.
